summary: The web app is a coherent product, not a pile of views: a real anonymous landing page (h1, features, pricing, CTAs), a working signup/login modal with 2FA and Turnstile, an auth-gated OS shell with 11 destinations, and genuinely good a11y infrastructure (global :focus-visible, reduced-motion, high-contrast, dyslexia mode, skip link, near-zero unnamed controls). The failures are concentrated in the first five minutes. The primary create-an-assignment flow is dead: NewAssignmentModal calls api.createAssignment, which does not exist on the api client, so the wizard always throws and renders an error box - blocking first value for every new account. The 150-token free trial promised at signup is activated only by TrialActivationCard, which is mounted only inside Billing, while the Dashboard the user lands on never shows it. Token cost is a hardcoded 420 with a dead Add-tokens button; the Billing balance is labelled Available Credits but shows tokens against a 10x-wrong plan table; 596 hardcoded pixel font sizes render most of the customer UI at 9-12px; and 21 modals declare aria-modal without trapping focus (measured: Tab escapes the signup dialog on the first press). Root cause across F1-F3 is an incomplete refactor - the shell was rebuilt but the creation call and the trial surface were never rewired. Headline fix: point the wizard at POST /api/assignments, render TrialActivationCard on the dashboard, and replace the fake cost and dead CTA with real values. No repo file was edited except this report; the uncommitted ChatBubble.jsx/main.jsx work was left untouched.

findings.title: Primary create-an-assignment flow is dead: api.createAssignment does not exist
findings.symptom: A new user clicks NEW STUDY SESSION (sidebar) or Import Assignment on an empty subject tile, completes the 3-step intake wizard, and on Initialize gets a red error box instead of an assignment. The one action the product is built around cannot complete.
findings.root_cause: web/src/components/NewAssignmentModal.jsx:111 calls api.createAssignment?.(payload).catch(...). The api object (web/src/api.js:330-335) exposes only get/post/put/delete/request; there is no createAssignment member, and the identifier appears exactly once in all of web/src. api.createAssignment is therefore undefined, the optional call yields undefined, and the chained .catch throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'catch'), caught at NewAssignmentModal.jsx:117-126 and rendered as errorText at :219-223. The backend endpoint it should call exists: POST /api/assignments (server/main.py:1314; AssignmentIn at server/main.py:757).
evidence: web/src/components/NewAssignmentModal.jsx:111 -- api.createAssignment?.(payload).catch(...)
measured: grep -rn createAssignment web/src -> exactly 1 hit, components/NewAssignmentModal.jsx:111; api.js contains no createAssignment
web/src/api.js:330-335 -- api members are get/post/put/delete/request plus named endpoints
server/main.py:1314 -- @app.post('/api/assignments'); AssignmentIn needs only title+prompt (server/main.py:757-764), both present in the payload built at NewAssignmentModal.jsx:100-109
findings.impact: Blocks first-run activation for every new account. Signup -> first assignment is the core loop; without it the dashboard is permanently empty and no token is ever consumed, so the trial and paywall are never reached.

findings.title: The free trial promised at signup is unreachable from where the user lands
findings.symptom: The signup modal says 'Start with a free 7-day trial - 150 task tokens' and the landing's primary CTA is Start Free Trial. After signup the user lands on Dashboard with a 0-token balance and no trial card; the activation card (2FA + 1-cent payment verification) renders only inside Billing.
findings.root_cause: TrialActivationCard is imported and rendered only at web/src/components/CreditsView.jsx:17 and :73. web/src/components/AssignmentCardDashboard.jsx (the default authed landing view, App.jsx:829) contains no reference to it.

web/src/components/AnonymousLanding.jsx:42 -- '7-day starter trial with 150 task tokens'; AuthModal signup copy promises the same
findings.impact: Zero-to-value dead end: the new user sees Import/Deploy CTAs everywhere with nothing to spend and no visible route to the trial that was the reason they signed up. Directly suppresses activation and therefore conversion.

findings.root_cause: web/src/components/NewAssignmentModal.jsx:48 hardcodes 'const tokenCost = 420' (used at :49, :108 token_estimate, :427). The remedy CTA at NewAssignmentModal.jsx:429-435 has type/className but no onClick or any handler.

web/src/components/EffortDial.jsx:13-15 -- per-turn figures 300/840/1800 tokens/turn are also static constants
web/src/components/AssignmentDumpView.jsx:638 -- the batch dump path does have a real 2-step spend confirmation, so the pattern exists elsewhere
findings.impact: A user cannot tell what an action will cost before doing it, and when short the only control offered is inert. Removes both cost transparency and the top-up funnel.

findings.title: Credit/token dual currency: mislabelled balance, two units side by side, 10x-wrong limit table
findings.symptom: The Billing balance strip is headed Available Credits but renders the token balance under the unit TOKENS. Sidebar and quick-settings show SYS_CREDITS and TOKENS (and cr) simultaneously. The low-credit warning compares credits against a table built on the token scale.
findings.root_cause: web/src/components/CreditsView.jsx:84 renders the label 'Available Credits' around CreditsView.jsx:96 tokenVal and :98 'TOKENS'. web/src/components/AppShell.jsx:332-342 renders SYS_CREDITS and TOKENS in one block; web/src/components/QuickSettings.jsx:115-121 renders credits 'cr' beside token_balance. web/src/App.jsx:746 uses planLimit {basic:30, pro:100, elite:280} || 30 and compares credits, while the plans grant 300/1000/2700 task tokens (AnonymousLanding.jsx:64,82,102) - a 10x scale error - and falls back to 30 for trial/none. Separately App.jsx:360/391 set plan 'none' while the 25s poll at App.jsx:491 falls back to 'basic', so the plan label can change on its own.

findings.title: 596 hardcoded pixel font sizes; the customer UI renders at 9-12px
findings.symptom: Metadata, chips, table cells, labels and helper text across the authenticated app render at 10px or 11px, some at 9px. The smallest rendered text is 9px ('Academic Co-pilot' in the sidebar).
findings.root_cause: Components use arbitrary Tailwind sizes instead of the design system's own type tokens. Counted: 596 occurrences of text-[Npx] across 9 distinct values - 327 at 10px, 215 at 11px, 47 at 9px. index.css defines a token scale (web/src/index.css:420-440) and a 16px base (index.css:481); the component code bypasses both.
evidence: measured: grep -rhoE text-[Npx] web/src --include=*.jsx -> 596 total; 327 @10px, 215 @11px, 47 @9px; 9 distinct values
web/src/index.css:481 -- html { font-size: 16px }
web/src/index.css:420-440 -- type tokens exist but are unused by components
measured (Playwright, authed dashboard) rendered text-node histogram: 3 nodes at 9px, 29 at 10px, 2 at 11px, 63 at 12px, 16 at 14px
measured (Playwright, anonymous landing): 1 node at 9px, 8 at 10px, 6 at 11px
findings.impact: Readability failure on every screen of a product whose users read dense text. Pixel sizing also defeats the browser minimum-font-size preference; WCAG 1.4.4 assumes text can be resized.

findings.title: 21 modals declare aria-modal but none traps focus - keyboard users tab into the page behind
findings.symptom: Open the signup dialog and press Tab once: focus moves to Start Free Trial behind the modal, then Read the Guide, Choose Basic, and on through the landing page. Focus never enters the dialog on open and is never contained.
findings.root_cause: Dialogs set role=dialog and aria-modal=true (web/src/components/AuthModal.jsx:369-370) but nothing implements a focus trap or inerts the background: grep across web/src/components for Tab-key handling, focus trap or inert returns zero hits, while 21 files declare aria-modal. The dependency radix-ui (web/package.json) is installed but imported nowhere in web/src, so the accessible dialog primitive that would fix this is available and unused.
evidence: measured (Playwright): with the signup dialog open (role=dialog, aria-modal=true, label 'Helpotron sign in'), 28 of 40 Tab presses focused an element OUTSIDE the dialog; the first 8 escapes were Start Free Trial, Read the Guide, Start free trial, Choose Basic, Choose Pro, Choose Elite, Start free, Privacy Policy
measured: grep for Tab-key handling / focusTrap / inert across web/src/components -> 0 hits
measured: grep -rn aria-modal web/src/components -> 21 hits across 21 files
measured: grep -rn radix web/src -> 0 hits, while radix-ui is a declared dependency (web/package.json)
findings.impact: aria-modal is a false promise on every dialog. Keyboard and screen-reader users can operate the page behind the modal and lose context; a WCAG 2.4.3 / focus-management failure affecting signup, payment, privacy and destructive-action dialogs.

findings.title: Global backend-unreachable banner can never render, and names the wrong port
findings.symptom: If the API is down while the browser is online, no app-level banner appears. The banner written for this case is dead code, and its remediation text points at the wrong port.
findings.root_cause: web/src/App.jsx:174 declares 'const [connected, setConnected] = useState(true)'; setConnected is never referenced anywhere in web/src, so connected is permanently true and the block at App.jsx:798-803 is unreachable. It also tells the operator to run '.venv/bin/uvicorn server.main:app --port 8000', while the API serves :5000 (project CONTEXT) via start_stack.sh. The remaining offline surface, OfflineBanner (web/src/components/ui/OfflineBanner.jsx:20-33), reacts only to navigator.onLine and a manual Force Reconnect fetch.
evidence: web/src/App.jsx:174 -- useState(true) for connected
measured: grep -rn setConnected web/src -> 1 hit, the declaration only
web/src/App.jsx:798-803 -- the unreachable block, including '--port 8000'
web/src/components/ui/OfflineBanner.jsx:20-33 -- online/offline events plus a manual /health fetch
findings.impact: A reachable browser with a dead API produces no global failure signal, so screens silently show empty or partial data. Any later fix would send an operator to a port nothing listens on.

findings.title: 34 hardcoded hex colours outside index.css contradict the 'zero hex literals in components' claim
findings.symptom: Some surfaces and charts ignore the theme: switching to light mode or high contrast leaves those elements on their dark-theme hardcoded colour.
findings.root_cause: web/src/index.css:6 claims 'Zero hex literals in components - all via CSS vars'. Counted outside index.css: 34 six-digit hex literals across jsx/js - components/CreditsCostTab.jsx 8 (duplicating #78f5e5/#59d8c9/#9aefea instead of using --st-primary or --chart-*), components/ui/background-beams.jsx 10 (vendored), lib/preferences.js 5, mock.js 3 (demo fixtures), MonitorsView.jsx 2, ActivityView.jsx 2, and four singletons.

web/src/components/CreditsCostTab.jsx:166-194 -- svg gradient and marker stops hardcode #78f5e5/#59d8c9/#9aefea
findings.impact: Theme and contrast modes are only partially honoured; a user switching to light or high-contrast gets inconsistent surfaces and the design system's own guard is unenforced.

findings.title: Light-theme muted text fails WCAG AA contrast (4.07-4.49:1) and is used at 10-11px
findings.symptom: In light mode, secondary and label text is hard to read, and it is the colour used for the smallest text on the page.
findings.root_cause: --text-muted resolves to --st-outline (web/src/index.css:275), which in the light theme is #6F7978 (index.css:210). Measured contrast: 4.07:1 on #F2F4F5 (surface-container-low), 4.28:1 on #F8FAFB (background), 4.49:1 on #FFFFFF - all below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal text. The dark theme passes comfortably (5.15-6.25:1).
evidence: web/src/index.css:210 -- light --st-outline: #6F7978
web/src/index.css:275 -- --text-muted: var(--st-outline)
measured (WCAG 2.x relative-luminance computation): #6F7978 on #F2F4F5 = 4.07; on #F8FAFB = 4.28; on #FFFFFF = 4.49
dark-theme control: #8E9192 on #0E1113 = 5.97; on #1D2024 = 5.15
findings.impact: AA contrast failure on secondary text in light mode, compounded by 10-11px sizing (H2-F5). Affects every user who switches to the light theme.

findings.title: Sandbox/demo toggle is exposed to every customer in the production top bar
findings.symptom: A paying or trial customer sees a SANDBOX / LIVE switch in the top bar; one click reloads the app into a fabricated dataset (demo assignments, courses, leaderboards), and a signed-out visitor can use it to view the authenticated shell.
findings.root_cause: DemoModeToggle is mounted unconditionally in the authed top bar at web/src/components/AppShell.jsx:424. The mock layer itself is well-guarded - opt-in only, never defaulting on (web/src/mock.js:15-25, web/src/demoData.js:37-44) and labelled by DemoRibbon - but web/src/mock.js:189 makes /api/me return 'authenticated: true' client-side while demo mode is on.
evidence: web/src/components/AppShell.jsx:424 -- DemoModeToggle in the top bar, visible to all users
web/src/mock.js:15-25 -- isDemoMode requires explicit 'on'/'true'; safe default
web/src/mock.js:189 -- the /api/me demo handler returns authenticated: true
web/src/components/DemoRibbon.jsx:26-38 -- the sandbox banner, rendered whenever demo mode is on
measured (Playwright, demo mode + token indicator): the authenticated shell booted with 11 sidebar items and the DEMO MODE ribbon visible
findings.impact: No real data is exposed - all fixtures are client-side - so this is a trust and clarity issue rather than a breach: a customer can mistake fabricated coursework for their own, and the paywall/shell can be previewed without an account. A debug affordance should not ship in the customer top bar.

findings.title: Agent-chat token telemetry is fabricated; uncommitted ChatBubble markdown change is sound but adds a circular chunk warning
findings.symptom: Per-message token figures in the agent chat are invented constants, so the cost feedback a user sees cannot be trusted. Separately, the uncommitted chat-rendering change produces a build warning.
findings.root_cause: web/src/components/MyAgentView.jsx hardcodes the token counts shown during and after generation - tokens: 120 at :351, 'tokens: res?.tokens_used || 420' at :453, tokens: 650 at :484, and a +15-per-event loop at :379 - never reconciled with the server's actual charge. The uncommitted work (web/src/main.jsx and web/src/components/ChatBubble.jsx) adds react-markdown/remark-math/rehype-katex and renders both user and assistant bubble text through ReactMarkdown.
evidence: web/src/components/MyAgentView.jsx:351, :379, :453, :484 -- hardcoded token counters
measured: git diff --numstat web/src -> ChatBubble.jsx +10/-3, main.jsx +1/-0 (uncommitted; left untouched, not reverted)
web/src/components/ChatBubble.jsx:2-4 imports; :91-93 and :113-115 ReactMarkdown wrappers; :90 and :112 add select-text
web/src/main.jsx:7 -- import 'katex/dist/katex.min.css'
measured: cd web && npm run build -> exit 0 in 27.76s, ONE warning 'Circular chunk: markdown -> vendor -> markdown'; dist/assets/markdown-TFpHTtqd.js 265.76 kB / gzip 79.46 kB
safety: react-markdown without rehype-raw escapes embedded HTML, so rendering user text as markdown is not an injection vector
findings.impact: The token numbers users rely on to judge spend are fiction, compounding the missing real cost estimate (H2-F3). The markdown change itself is a genuine improvement (math and formatting in chat, selectable text); the warning is a chunking smell, not a correctness bug.

fixes.change: Replace the line 'const res = await api.createAssignment?.(payload).catch(() => ({ id: ..., ...payload }));' with 'const res = await api.post("/api/assignments", payload);'. api.post already JSON-stringifies the body (web/src/api.js:331) and the endpoint exists (server/main.py:1314). Delete the fabricated-success .catch fallback entirely so the existing catch at :117-126 surfaces the real error and never a phantom assignment. If AssignmentIn rejects the client's extra keys (subject/course_name/status/token_estimate), map the payload explicitly to {title, due_date, prompt} rather than widening the schema.
fixes.risk: The /api/assignments route is the extension scrape-save path; if it needs canvas_id or >=200 chars in prompt to kick the agent, short manual intakes may 422 or create a card with no team launched. Verify the response and surface it honestly.
fixes.verify: cd web && npm run build; then click NEW STUDY SESSION, complete steps 1-3, Initialize. Before: errorText reads 'Cannot read properties of undefined'. After: step 4 renders and no red error box appears. Static: grep -n createAssignment web/src/components/NewAssignmentModal.jsx returns nothing.

external_research.what: W3C - What's New in WCAG 2.2 (SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 2.5.8 Target Size 24x24 AA, 1.4.4 Resize Text, 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured)
external_research.why: Settles the two a11y claims in this report. (a) There is NO minimum font size in WCAG - 10px is a design judgment, not a violation - but 1.4.4 requires text to be resizable and warns against pixel-locked sizing, which is exactly what the 596 text-[Npx] sites do. (b) The 21 modals' lack of a focus trap plus a first-Tab escape is a 2.4.7 / focus-management failure, and 2.5.8 clarifies the 24x24 target expectation for the small icon-only controls found in the shell.
external_research.verdict: adopt - use SC 2.4.7 and 1.4.4 as the review criteria for H2-X5 and H2-X6, and stop citing a non-existent minimum font size in the fix notes.

external_research.what: Userpilot / Skene / GTM Vault - SaaS activation, empty-state and reverse-trial benchmarks (2024-2026)
external_research.why: Quantifies the cost of H2-F1 and H2-F2. Reported medians: ~60-70% of signups never reach activation, cross-SaaS activation ~37.5%, median activation ~30% (Lenny survey); every 1% of activation correlates with ~2% lower churn; card-optional trials convert at 8-25% (median ~15-18.5%) vs 30-60% for card-required. A 7-day / 150-token trial is a short value window, which makes the missing in-product activation path and the broken first action directly revenue-affecting rather than cosmetic.
external_research.license: vendor blog / commercial research (numbers are directional, not auditable)
external_research.verdict: adapt - use the direction (fix first-action and first-value path before any paywall tuning) and measure our own cohort rather than treating the multipliers as targets.

external_research.what: Empty-state / first-run onboarding patterns (Candu, Simplileap case study, Thoughtlytics)
external_research.why: The app's default subjects render six empty states, each with an Import Assignment CTA, and no single first action or progress cue. The literature says pre-loaded sample data plus one primary action lifts activation, and - importantly for H2-F10 - that sample data MUST be labelled as sample data or users delete the wrong record. The 07-2025 Simplileap case (blank dashboard, integration required before value, skipped tours -> 7-day activation 11%->29%) is the same failure shape as this app's dashboard.
external_research.verdict: adapt - adopt 'one primary action + honest sample-data label' for the dashboard, which we already have in DemoRibbon (H2-F10 should keep that label, not remove it).

external_research.what: React a11y / focus-visible guidance and radix-ui (already a dependency in web/package.json, imported nowhere in web/src)
external_research.why: The fix for H2-F6 needs a focus-trapping dialog primitive. Radix Dialog is already installed and provides focus trap, focus restore, background inert and Escape handling; the codebase has none of those (0 hits). Adopting it is a wiring change, not a new dependency.
external_research.verdict: adopt - swap the hand-rolled role=dialog/aria-modal shell for Radix Dialog across the 21 dialogs, starting with AuthModal and the payment/privacy/destructive confirms.
